target.title: Gary Habermas - Chapter 004 - The Resurrection Connection to All of Life - Gary Habermas @Sean McDowell
target.domain: popular Christian apologetics / pastoral theology (auto-captioned interview transcript)
target.comparison_class: paper of similar purpose and evidence burden
target.population_boundary: Two named speakers (Habermas, McDowell) and persons they explicitly represent (Habermas's wives, children, students Ben Shaw/Mike Licona, critics, persecuted Christians in Nigeria, Ukraine); no independent corroboration available

gate_results.rationale: Historical claims (resurrection, apostolic preaching, Paul's suffering lists) are asserted with scripture citation but no traceable external evidence in-document; the minimal-facts method is named (S158) but not executed. Not a hard FAIL because the genre is interview/pastoral, not an evidential treatise, and the source itself flags the evidential volumes as elsewhere.

Speaker explicitly grants possible gospel errors (S149-S152) while denying them (S222) — an acknowledged, bounded tension he names and works around rather than conceals; no load-bearing unresolved contradiction.
gate_results.resolution: Tension acknowledged and bounded by the minimal-facts move.

gate_results.rationale: Conclusions about resurrection's centrality to 'virtually every major doctrine' (S057) exceed what the interview evidences; near-death-experience claim 'almost irrefutable' (S352) is asserted outside its evidential support.
Speaker states what would count against him: 'if there's no resurrection... it's gullible' (S581-S582) and invites refutation (S583).

Cross-domain bridge from historical resurrection to pastoral practice (suffering, doubt, fear of death) is asserted by analogy ('many faceted diamond', S047/S263) without explicit mapping or kill condition.
Auto-captioned transcript with caption errors (S014 'Gary Hermos', S092 'Ephesians 289', S162 'Craig Bombberg'); quotations of scripture and of Ellis/Wesley are paraphrased, not cited precisely.
No concealed compulsion; the guest discloses his own grief and doubt voluntarily (S113-S114, S534), the interviewer asks permission (S532-S534), and no outcome is produced by coercion.
